blocks.title: Question.2
blocks.question:
Blood group Antigen are :-

(1) Found in Hb molecule

(2) Found in Plasma protein

(3) Found on RBC

(4) None
blocks.answer:
Ans= 3

Explanation:

Blood group antigens are specific markers or molecules that are found on the surface of red blood cells (RBCs). These antigens determine an individual's blood group, such as A, B, AB, or O, and also determine compatibility in blood transfusions. The two main systems for blood typing are the ABO system and the Rh system, where the presence or absence of certain antigens (like A, B, or Rh) on the RBC surface defines the blood group.

blocks.title: Question.3
blocks.question:
Blood colloidal osmotic pressure mainly maintained by which plasma protein :-

(1) Globulin

(2) Albumin

(3) Fibrinogen

(4) Prothrombin
blocks.answer:
The correct answer is:
(2) Albumin

Explanation:

Blood colloidal osmotic pressure (also known as oncotic pressure) is primarily maintained by albumin, a type of plasma protein. Albumin helps to retain water in the blood vessels by exerting an osmotic pull, which prevents excessive loss of fluid from the blood into the surrounding tissues. This is crucial in maintaining proper blood volume and pressure.

blocks.text:
• Rh antigen found on the surface of RBC.

    • Rh antigen is due to dominant gene. So if one of the gamete possess gene for  Rh factor, its offspring would be Rh⁺.
    • On the basis of presence or absence of Rh antigen blood group can be positive(+) or negative(-)
    • If receiver is positive and donor is negative, then transfusion is always safe.
    • If receiver is negative and donor is positive, then only first transfusion is safe.

blocks.title: Question-1
blocks.question:
Persons with 'AB' blood group are called as "Universal recipients". This is due to :

(1) Absence of antigens A and B on the surface of RBCs

(2) Absence of antigens A and B in plasma

(3) Presence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, on RBCs

(4) Absence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, in plasma
blocks.answer:
Answer: 4

Explanation:

People with AB blood group are referred to as universal recipients because they can receive blood from any ABO blood group without having an immune reaction. This is because individuals with AB blood do not have anti-A or anti-B antibodies in their plasma. As a result, they can accept red blood cells from any donor (A, B, AB, or O) without the risk of antibody-mediated destruction of the donor's RBCs.
options: (1) Absence of antigens A and B on the surface of RBCs
(2) Absence of antigens A and B in plasma
(3) Presence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, on RBCs
(4) Absence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, in plasma

blocks.title: Question-1
blocks.question:
Closed circulatory system occurs in

(1) Cockroach

(2) Tadpole/Fish

(3) Mosquito

(4) Housefly
blocks.answer:
Answer :  2

Explanation:

A closed circulatory system is one where the blood is contained within blood vessels, and it circulates throughout the body. This type of circulatory system is found in vertebrates, including fish/tadpole.

blocks.title: Question-2
blocks.question:
Systemic heart refers to :-

(1) The heart that contracts under stimulation from nervous system

(2) Left auricle and left ventricle in higher vertebrates

(3) Entire heart in lower vertebrates

(4) The two ventricles together in humans
blocks.answer:
Ans= 2

Explanation:

The systemic heart refers to the left side of the heart, which consists of the left auricle (atrium) and the left ventricle in higher vertebrates, including humans. This part of the heart is responsible for pumping oxygenated blood to the body through the aorta.
options: (1) The heart that contracts under stimulation from nervous system
(2) Left auricle and left ventricle in higher vertebrates
(4) The two ventricles together in humans

blocks.title: Example-2
blocks.question:
Q.2 Bicuspid (mitral) valve guards the opening in mammals between :-

(1) Left atrium and left ventricle

(2) Pulmonary vein and left auricle

(3) Stomach and intestine

(4) Right atrium and right ventricle
blocks.answer:
Answer : 1

Explanation:

The bicuspid (mitral) valve is a type of atrioventricular valve that guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle in mammals. This valve ensures that blood flows in one direction, from the left atrium to the left ventricle, and prevents backflow of blood into the atrium when the ventricle contracts.

blocks.title: Cardiac Cycle
blocks.text:
• One complete rhythmic relaxation and contraction of all the parts of the heart which result in receiving and pumping of the blood is cardiac cycle
  • Duration of cardiac cycle = 60/72 = 0.8 sec.
  • Adult human: 72 cardiac cycle/min
  • End Diastolic Volume (EDV) = 120 ml.
  • End Systolic Volume (ESV) = 50 ml.
  • Stroke Volume (SV) = EDV – ESV = 120 - 50 = 70 ml.
  • Stroke Volume (SV) = Amount of blood pumped by each ventricle in one cardiac cycle.
  • Cardiac Output = SV × Number of beats/min
  • Cardiac cycle = 1 / heart beat per minute
  • Heart Beat:Rhythmic pulsation of musculature of the heart (Human Adults : 72;New Born Baby:>120
  • Number of pulse = Number of cardiac cycle.
  • Pulse is easily felt in the radial artery of the wrist and carotid artery of neck.
Different Events during Cardiac cycle:

blocks.title: Question.1
blocks.question:
The heart sound "DUP" is produced when :-

(1) Mitral valve opens

(2) Mitral valve closes

(3) Semilunar valve at the base of aorta closes

(4) Tricuspid valve opens
blocks.answer:
Ans= 3

Explanation:

The heart sounds "LUB" and "DUP" are produced during the cardiac cycle:

  • "LUB" is the first sound, produced when the atrioventricular (AV) valves (mitral and tricuspid) close at the beginning of ventricular contraction.
  • "DUP" is the second sound, produced when the semilunar valves (pulmonary and aortic valves) close at the beginning of ventricular relaxation. This occurs after the blood has been pumped out into the arteries.
options: (3) Semilunar valve at the base of aorta closes

blocks.title: Question.2
blocks.question:
Tachycardia is :-

(1) Fast heart rate

(2) Slow heart rate

(3) Stop heart rate

(4) Normal heart rate
blocks.answer:
Ans= 1

Explanation:

Tachycardia refers to a condition where the heart rate is faster than normal, typically defined as a heart rate above 100 beats per minute in adults. This can occur due to various factors such as exercise, stress, fever, or certain medical conditions.

blocks.title: ECG
blocks.text:
Blood pressure:

  • Pressure exerted by the flowing blood on the elastic walls of arteries.
  • Instrument: Sphygmomanometer.
  • Two stages :-i) Systolic pressure (120 mm of Hg)
(ii) Diastolic pressure (80 mm of Hg)

blocks.title: Hepatic portal system
blocks.text:
• Unique vascular connection between the digestive tract and liver called hepatic portal system.
  • The hepatic portal vein carries blood from intestine to the liver before it is delivered to the systemic circulation.

blocks.title: Disorders
blocks.text:
Disorders:

  • Hypertension / High blood pressure BP  is 140/90 mm of Hg or higher.Leads to heart diseases. Affects vital organs like Brain, Kidney.
  • Coronary artery disease (CAD) / Atherosclerosis : Caused by deposition of calcium, fat, cholesterol and fibrous tissue in coronary arteries, which makes the lumen of arteries narrow.
  • Angina / Angina Pectoris : Acute chest pain,Not enough oxygen is reaching the heart muscles, Most common in middle aged and elderly
  • Heart Failure : Heart is not pumping blood effectively enough to meet the needs of the body.
  • Cardiac arrest : When the heart stops beating.
• Heart attack : Heart muscles is suddenly damaged by an inadequate blood supply.

blocks.title: Question-1
blocks.question:
The T wave in an ECG represents:
1) Atrial depolarization
2) Ventricular depolarization
3) Ventricular repolarization
4) Atrial repolarization
blocks.answer:
Answer: 3) Ventricular repolarization

The T wave in an ECG represents the repolarization of the ventricles, which is the recovery phase where the ventricles return to their resting state after contraction.

The T wave in an ECG represents:

2) Ventricular depolarization

4) Atrial repolarization

blocks.title: Question.2
blocks.question:
Blood Capillaries are made of :-

(1) Endothelium and thin coat of connective tissue

(2) Endothelium and thin coat of muscle fibres

(3) Endothelium and thin coat of connective tissue and muscle fibres.

(4) Only endothelium
blocks.answer:
The correct answer is:
(4)Only endothelium

Explanation:

Blood capillaries are the smallest blood vessels in the body, and their walls are primarily made up of:

  • Endothelium: A single layer of endothelial cells that allows the exchange of gases, nutrients, and waste products between the blood and surrounding tissues.
options: (1) Endothelium and thin coat of connective tissue
(2) Endothelium and thin coat of muscle fibres
(3) Endothelium and thin coat of connective tissue and muscle fibres.
